## THE FAILURE STORY

Development ran hot across the 10 worktrees during July 15-18. Three worktrees (branched from system_v5) began importing from CB.cache, CB.validation, CB.metrics, CB.async_queue, and CB.security—libraries that were documented in the CB integration spec and appeared in early design discussions. No one on those teams realized only 28 of the 33 CB libraries had actually been wired into the codebase. The integration tracker showed green because it counted "specifications written" as "implemented." By July 18, across 43 commits touching 492 files, the system_v5 subsystem alone had 87 new imports from the five unwired libraries.

The first merge attempt to main happened in early August. Tests ran locally on individual branches without issue (each branch existed in isolation with its own virtual environment). When the July work was consolidated, runtime initialization hit ImportError on `from CB.cache import CacheLayer` in system_v5's startup sequence. The fallback caught it as AttributeError downstream when code tried to instantiate the missing objects. The person merging stopped the push. By then, 23 of the 43 commits were half-integrated into a feature branch; rolling back required untangling interdependent changes across five worktrees. The v9 main branch—already 6,637 lines of JSON scaffolding—could not accommodate the necessary rewiring. The project lost a week to manual dependency surgery.

## THE UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION

The team assumed the CB integration status board reflected actual codebase availability, not just specification completion.

## EARLY WARNING SIGNS

1. **During July 15-18 development:** Developers on different worktrees working offline; no real-time cross-branch import validation. First person to run the consolidated build is the first to hit the error.

2. **Before merge:** No pre-merge dependency audit step. A scan of all `from CB.*` imports against the wired-library list would have surfaced all five missing libraries before code touched main.
